historical_growth.growth_rate_source: pre-COVID FY2016-FY2019 revenue CAGR (4.6%) tempered to 4.0%; FY26 revenue +2.5%, TTV +4.7%, plus Iglu consolidation in FY27
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Every 3- and 5-year CAGR spans the COVID trough (FY2021 revenue 396m vs 3,055m in FY2019; negative EPS FY2020-FY2022) and describes recovery, not growth. Revenue 5yr 48.5%, EPS 3yr 45.4% and owner-FCF CAGRs are arithmetic artefacts and were not used. Over 7 and 10 years revenue is flat to slightly down: FLT has not yet regained FY2019 revenue despite TTV above the 2019 peak, because revenue margin fell from ~13% to 11.1% of TTV. Equity CAGRs are negative/low because of the COVID losses and buy-backs.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest income) is extremely lumpy: 3.3 / 277.1 / -5.5 / 142.6 for FY23-FY26, driven by client-float working-capital timing. This is why the forward build is component-based (EBITDA -> lease -> D&A -> tax -> capex) rather than a margin carried forward.

scenario_narratives.base: TTV grows mid-single digits on cruise (Iglu, Norwegian charter, cruise TTV >A$2bn in FY27), corporate wins (FCM, Corporate Traveller) and a leisure network that has stopped shrinking; revenue margin holds near 11% of TTV so revenue grows 4-5% then decays to 2.5%. The Pillar cost-out and AI co-consulting tools lift the EBITDA margin 1.5pp over six years to 15.5%, well short of the pre-COVID structure. Cash tax normalises to 30% as the COVID deferred tax assets are consumed. Capex stays ~3.3% of revenue (mostly software). Buy-backs continue but are value-neutral here.
scenario_narratives.bull: Corporate share gains accelerate (productive-operations automation lets FCM/CT win mid-market accounts at lower cost), the cruise pivot scales faster than planned, and leisure recovers revenue margin through World360 Rewards and higher-attach luxury/Scott Dunn product. Revenue compounds 8% fading to 3%; EBITDA margin reaches 17% (still below the FY2019 equivalent), lease cost shrinks as the shop network is rationalised, and the float grows with TTV (8% capture). Nothing here requires a re-rating - the cap stays at 13x.
scenario_narratives.bear: A demand shock in year 2 - recession, a wider Middle East conflict (FCM UAE TTV already fell ~15% in FY26), an aviation capacity or health event - cuts revenue 6% with fixed lease and staff costs: EBITDA margin drops to 11.5% and cash tax falls to 20%. The recovery is partial because online direct booking and airline NDC keep eroding revenue margin, leaving margins at 13% and growth at 2%. Terminal growth 2%. The A$200m 2027 notes are refinanced from the 570m unrestricted cash; solvency is not the bear case, permanent margin loss is.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Flight Centre's history is split by COVID: FY2016-FY2019 is a mature 15-16% (pre-IFRS16) margin travel agent, FY2020-FY2022 is near-zero revenue and ~A$1.4bn of cumulative losses funded by two equity raises and convertible notes, and FY2023-FY2026 is the recovery. No trailing CAGR is usable - the 3- and 5-year figures describe the bounce off the trough - so the DCF is a component build anchored on FY2026's clean cash economics: statutory EBITDA with non-cash gains stripped (14.0% of revenue, gross of SBC), lease cash charged in the flows (treatment B), D&A ex right-of-use, cash tax ramping from 26% to 30% as COVID deferred tax assets are used, and capex at ~3.3% of revenue. FY2026 is not a peak - underlying PBT of 278m is below FY2019's 343m on the same revenue and the post-IFRS16 equivalent of the FY2019 margin is ~19-20% - so a modest recovery to 15.5% is the base, not a mid-cycle haircut. Risk is charged once: one 9.5% AUD WACC, a 13x terminal cap for a cyclical, and a 25/50/25 weighting with a year-2 demand shock in the bear. Net debt follows FLT's own capital-management definition (unrestricted cash and investments less borrowings) but adds the convertible notes at face (650m), which FLT excludes; restricted client cash (255m) and lease liabilities (352m) are excluded consistently.
key_risks_to_valuation: Revenue margin (revenue/TTV) has fallen from ~13% pre-COVID to 11.1%; further erosion from airline NDC/direct distribution and online leisure competition would make the margin ramp unattainable even if TTV grows.

Demand shocks: travel is the first discretionary spend cut in a recession and is exposed to geopolitical and health events; FY26 already absorbed a ~A$60m leisure profit hit from the Middle East conflict.
FLT has booked 'underlying adjustments' of 64-76m every year since COVID; if restructuring costs are permanent, the 14.0% clean anchor is itself generous and the ramp to 15.5% does not happen.

Client float: 824.8m of cash includes 254.5m restricted and the remainder partly funds 567m of client creditors; a TTV contraction reverses the float (modelled only through wc_capture x negative revenue change in the bear).

Convertible notes: 200m due Nov-2027 and 450m due Sep-2032 (strike A$15.88, put Sep-2030). Treated as debt at face; if the shares re-rate above the strikes the dilution (~28m shares on the 2032 notes) replaces the debt, roughly neutral at those prices.
Capex (3.3% of revenue) has exceeded D&A ex-ROU (2.6%) for three years; if software capitalisation is really maintenance, owner FCF is structurally lower than NOPAT suggests.
Acquisition cadence: Iglu (~180m) in FY26, Scott Dunn earlier; the model assumes organic growth only and no further M&A cash outflow.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 9.61-16.56
data_sources.financials: FLT.AX_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, adjudicated 2026-09-22) plus FLT.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt: cash flow statement (lines 2213-2265), balance sheet (2273-2333), Appendix 4E statutory-to-underlying reconciliation (96-131), note B5 convertible notes (3588-3617), note B6 net cash/(debt) (3631-3659), note D4 share capital (4755-4787), note F7 right-of-use depreciation (5314), share-based payments expense (5617), EPS denominators (4999-5003)
data_sources.qualitative: FY26 Annual Report directors' report and outlook (lines 289-480), H1 FY26 interim (capital management, AI rollout). No Analysis JSON existed at build time; FY27 guidance is due at the November 2026 AGM.

inputs.share_count_basis: 206,156,256 ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (FY26 AR note D4, after the 11.75m buy-back) plus ~4.15m dilutive rights (diluted 214.51m less basic 210.36m weighted average, note on EPS). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. Convertible notes (2027 strike A$18.59, 2032 strike A$15.88) are out of the money and treated as debt at face, not as dilution. The further A$200m buy-back announced 17 June 2026 is value-neutral in this model.
inputs.net_debt_note: total_debt = borrowings 333.471 (25.106 current + 308.365 non-current, FY26 AR B4) + convertible notes at FACE 650.0 (A$200m Nov-2027 + A$450m Sep-2032; carrying value 548.965 accretes to face at 7.0%/8.2% EIR). cash = unrestricted cash 570.220 + non-current financial investments 17.173, per FLT's own Net cash/(debt) note B6. EXCLUDED: 254.535 restricted client cash (824.755 total less 570.220) and lease liabilities 352.418 (treatment B, charged in the flows). NCI 3.415 ignored (immaterial).
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 AR share-based payments expense note: 16,162 (FY25 11,226; FY24 12,484), A$ thousands. Cash settlement runs through 'Payments for purchase of shares on market' (20.6m) in financing. No net-share-settlement tax in Australia.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest received 24.5m (cash flow statement) stripped because unrestricted cash is added back in the bridge; P&L interest income 23.9m.
inputs.buyback_note: Payments for share buy-back 142.859m in FY26 (57.125m in FY25). The count is being funded by a repurchaser.
inputs.last_fcf_note: last_fcf = reported FCF (OCF 277.935 - PPE 32.078 - intangibles 62.565 = 183.292) - SBC 16.162 - interest income 24.5. Under lease treatment B the component build additionally charges lease principal (83.427) inside EBITDA, so the like-for-like FY26 unlevered owner FCF is ~87m (142.6 - 83.4 principal + 28.0 non-lease interest paid). FY26 also carried ~85m of cash restructuring/loyalty-launch costs and a ~36m working-capital outflow; the component build starts at year 1 without crediting either.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD flows discounted at an AUD rate: 10y ACGB ~4.3% + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.3 = ~11.5% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~6% (bank facilities; CN coupons 2.5% but EIR 7-8%), 4.2% after tax; ~29% debt weight on EV = 9.4%, rounded to 9.5%. ONE WACC for all three scenarios: cyclicality, geopolitical shocks and margin risk are in the bear flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: B (leases as operating cost): lease principal 83.427 + lease interest 16.588 = 100.0m (3.5% of revenue) charged inside adjusted EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities 352.418 EXCLUDED from net debt; D&A for cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation (161.358 - 86.101 = 75.257, 2.64% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI 3.415m on the balance sheet, NCI profit share 0.165m: immaterial, not deducted.
inputs.ebitda_anchor_note: FY26 statutory EBITDA 430.562 includes non-cash gains (Global Hotels sale 15.217, contingent consideration reversal 15.753, Pedal JV 18.892, CN buy-back 0.09) and one-off acquisition costs 3.973. Stripping those and adding back the 16.162 SBC expense (the engine deducts SBC separately) gives 400.8m = 14.0% of revenue, which is the year-1 anchor. It gives NO credit for the 81.3m of 'Pillar initiatives' (47.4) and 'Leisure Loyalty Program' (33.9) costs FLT excludes from its 465.9 underlying EBITDA, because FLT has booked such adjustments every year since COVID (FY25: 76.4m). The base ramp to 15.5% by year 6 is where those fade and productivity shows up; post-IFRS16 equivalent FY2019 margin was ~19-20%.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (routed via dcf-methods: non-US cyclical operating company -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Flight Centre is a leisure and corporate travel agency; revenue is ~11% of TTV (A$25.7bn FY26). COVID collapsed FY2020-FY2022 (revenue 396m FY21, cumulative losses ~1.4bn, two equity raises 101m -> 199m shares, convertible notes) and FY2023-FY2026 is the recovery. None of the trough years is a usable base: the build is anchored on FY26 clean cash economics and projects a mid-cycle margin path, not a CAGR off the trough. First valuation of this ticker; fresh build, no reconciliation block.

base.growth_note: Y1 5% = FY26 organic 2.5% plus a full year of Iglu (acquired FY26, ~180m cash) and the Norwegian cruise charter; record July TTV. Decays to 2.5% terminal.
base.margin_note: Starts at the FY26 clean margin (14.0%, gross of SBC, post-IFRS16) and adds 0.3pp/yr to 15.5% as Pillar cost-out and AI co-consulting productivity come through. Still ~4pp below the FY2019 post-IFRS16 equivalent.
base.tax_note: Cash tax 26% in Y1 (FY26 cash tax 50.8m on 213m PBT = 24%, 288m of deferred tax assets from COVID losses) ramping to the 30% Australian statutory rate by Y5.
base.wc_note: Travel agent float: customers pay before suppliers; 5% of the revenue increase captured as cash. Positive sign because payables (2,162m) exceed receivables + contract assets (1,683m).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because travel demand is cyclical and shock-prone (COVID, Middle East, aviation events) and FLT's cost base is largely fixed within a year; bull cut from 35% to 25% because the bull case needs cruise scale-up, corporate wins AND margin recovery to coincide while structural revenue-margin erosion continues. Solvency is not in play (570m unrestricted cash vs 333m borrowings), so the bear is a margin/growth case rather than a going-concern one.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
